findings.message: The popup-conversion collection is incomplete. The source states that only login and registration retain page-based verification, while the scene inventory explicitly includes forgot-password verification. Therefore forgot password falls within the non-login/registration scenarios that must use a verification popup. findings.message: The popup-conversion collection incorrectly excludes the forgot-password verification flow. The rule exempts only login and registration, while the scene inventory explicitly includes 忘记密码. R-028's claim that it remains page-based relies on an unanchored “用户确认” and contradicts the supplied source. Add the forgot-password verification flow as an affected popup surface and evidence target.

No candidate requirement or handoff covers proactive SMS delivery monitoring and alerting, including awareness of carrier-side daily limits. R-021 covers routing, fallback and queryable channel status, but those do not satisfy the source's separate requirement for active arrival-rate, latency and failure-rate monitoring and alerts.

The delayed-code/resend ambiguity is not covered. The source identifies that a resend creates a new code while an older code may still be in transit, causing users to receive multiple codes without knowing which is valid. The four-state button and cooldown only prevent clicks during the cooldown; they do not define behavior after cooldown or provide an explicit backend follow-up for code issuance/validity semantics.

R-001 merges a Web implementation change with the independent App no-change regression obligation, while R-031 separately duplicates that App obligation. R-001 has collectionSemantics=none and only the Web surface S-001, so its doing status and evidence cannot independently represent its App assertion. Split the Web and App requirements cleanly or remove the duplicated App clause from R-001.

The switch-method prototype visibly requires the current method row to have a distinct selected/highlighted treatment (the email row has the emphasized blue border) in addition to the 【当前】 badge. R-004 captures the badge but omits this visible selected-state requirement and therefore provides no explicit evidence expectation for it.

R-028 incorrectly excludes the forgot-password verification flow based on an unattached “user confirmation.” The source states that only login and registration retain page form, that all other verification scenarios become popups, and explicitly lists forgot password. Add an implement surface and evidence for forgot-password popup conversion, or record an explicit source-backed conflict resolution.

The login-switch requirements remain internally contradictory. Detailed requirements and the review record require a real switch entry/dialog on Web and App, while acceptance rows require Web to show no switch entry and App to remain unchanged. R-002/R-003/R-019 unilaterally declare the acceptance rows superseded without a source unit establishing that precedence. Preserve this as an open clarification or provide a source-backed precedence rule.

R-012 does not retain the acceptance requirement that the successful-send button visibly becomes “验证码已发送” plus the icon. It instead specifies only “倒计时+icon,” leaving the exact visible sent-state label uncovered. Capture the label explicitly while keeping the dynamic remaining time in the tooltip as required by R-013.

The backend/channel handoff omits concrete channel-management obligations: remove/filter unused channels and define automatic routing using country, carrier, or email-suffix information. R-021's generic “渠道优化/自动降级” wording does not preserve these source semantics or identify corresponding affected surfaces.

R-021 combines independently deliverable and independently verifiable work—channel filtering/routing, automatic fallback and resend, ten-minute validity, manual 3–5 minute SOP with withdrawal/reversal, and third-party status diagnostics—under one requirement and one bundled backend surface. Split these obligations or model them as an explicit member collection with separate owners, surfaces, and evidence contracts.

Surface ID S-077 is reused with incompatible meanings: R-007 defines it as the iOS shared security-verification component, while R-008 defines it as a generic App popup-conversion assessment. This makes both explicit-set counts and handoff/evidence mapping ambiguous. Assign distinct stable surface IDs and state the iOS/Android membership for R-008.

R-018 requires inspection and correction of every App SMS-code input entry, but declares collectionSemantics=none and provides only one generic surface. The whole-source scope includes both iOS and Android, and the source explicitly says all SMS verification-code inputs. Enumerate the platform/entry matrix or identify authoritative shared controls whose coverage proves the collection complete.

R-006 lists pure-logic, component-dom, and copy-literal evidence, but implement surfaces S-095 through S-099 are covered only by aggregate contract-or-scenario-tests/typecheck commands (E-85, E-86, E-88). Those command kinds do not satisfy the listed evidence types for the registration, login, withdrawal, password, and other-sensitive-operation consumers. Add plan-conforming consumer integration/DOM evidence (and applicable copy evidence), or revise the evidence plan with a justified matching kind.

The popup-conversion collection is incomplete. The source states that only login and registration retain page-based verification, while the scene inventory explicitly includes forgot-password verification. Therefore forgot password falls within the non-login/registration scenarios that must use a verification popup. R-028 instead marks it not applicable based on an unsupported “user confirmation,” and R-007 has no implementing surface or evidence command for this flow. Add the forgot-password verification surface to the popup collection and provide corresponding evidence.
